item.title: Court Rejects Atiku’s Bid To Tender Fresh Evidence In Suit Seeking Tinubu’s Disqualification
item.description: Justice Inyang Ekwo of the Federal High Court in Abuja has dismissed an application by former Vice President and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, to present fresh evidence in his suit seeking to prevent President Bola Tinubu from contesting the 2027 presidential election over allegations of forgery of his National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) discharge certificate. The judge held that the time allowed by law to present evidence in a pre-election suit was 14 days, in line with Section 285(9) of the 1999 Constitution. Justice Ekwo agreed with Tinubu and the other defendants that allowing Atiku to introduce fresh evidence would alter the nature of the original case and violate the provisions of the Constitution. In his ruling on Atiku’s application to amend the originating summons in the suit against Tinubu, the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), the judge held that the former vice president attempted to mislead the court by claiming that the proposed amendment would not introduce fresh issues. Justice Ekwo said that, after carefully examining the application, the court found that the ADC presidential candidate sought to substitute existing evidence with new evidence which, if allowed, would circumvent Section 285(9) of the Constitution, which requires such evidence to be presented within 14 days. A man walks past the Federal High Court premises in Abuja, on April 22, 2026. (Photo by LIGHT ORIYE TAMUNOTONYE / AFP) According to the judge, allowing Atiku to introduce fresh evidence through the back door would amount to a fundamental injustice against the defendants. Meanwhile, following an agreement among the lawyers, the judge fixed December 2 for the hearing of the substantive suit. Atiku had told the court that he needed to make substantial amendments to his case challenging Tinubu’s eligibility to participate in the 2027 presidential election. In the main suit, Atiku and the ADC asked Justice Ekwo to disqualify Tinubu and the APC from the 2027 presidential election. They challenged the authenticity of Tinubu’s NYSC discharge certificate submitted to INEC by the APC. The plaintiffs, who sued the president, the APC and INEC as the first to third defendants, respectively, in an originating summons marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1888/2026, alleged that the APC submitted a forged NYSC discharge certificate belonging to the president to INEC. INEC Headquarters in Abuja. They, therefore, asked the court to compel INEC to remove Tinubu’s name and that of the APC from the list of candidates and political parties for the presidential election. However, Tinubu and the APC, in a joint counter-affidavit filed on September 9, urged the court to dismiss the suit in its entirety for being incompetent, arguing that the plaintiffs lacked the legal right to institute the case. They denied submitting any forged certificate to INEC for either the 2023 or 2027 presidential elections. T

‘That’s Not What’s Driving Me’: Tonye Cole Denies Trading Support For Future APC Governorship Ticket
item.description: Former Rivers State governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Tonye Cole, has denied that his decision to support the party’s political arrangement ahead of the 2027 elections was motivated by a promise of a future governorship ticket. Cole said his priority was to change the perception of Rivers State as a place associated with violence and political strongmen, arguing that peace and security were essential to attracting investment to the state. He spoke on Friday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief , where he was asked whether he had been promised an opportunity to pursue his governorship ambition in the future. “No, and that is not what is driving me,” he replied. “What is driving me is that if you cannot bring peace and security and change the narrative of Rivers State, investment will not come to Rivers State. So the first aspect of it is that we must change the mindset of everyone that when they talk about Rivers State, violence, strongman, no gentlemen, loud, all of that tagline must change. “If I cannot be the face of what the future of Rivers State politics should look like, then we have a problem,” he added. ﻿ Cole, who emerged as the APC governorship candidate in 2019 and 2023, withdrew from the party’s 2027 governorship race in May following consultations and efforts to reconcile rival factions within the state chapter. He subsequently aligned with the Rainbow Coalition, a cross-party political arrangement led by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, which is backing President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. Explaining his decision to remain with the APC group that predated the current political arrangement, Cole said he wanted to ensure that members who had worked to build the party were not sidelined. “For me, abandoning those who were in APC who worked was not the question. So I decided that I was going to stay with them so that they would have a voice. They cannot be removed, so I stayed there to represent the voice of the APC that built forth and kept Rivers State whole,” he said. He added that the decision to bring different political interests together was informed by the need to prevent divisions that had previously weakened the APC in Rivers State. ‘No Differences With Wike’ A combo of Cole, Wike, and logos of the APC and PDP Wike holds near-total control over the formal political institutions and party structures in Rivers State. There was intense, public friction and even a defamation lawsuit between Cole and the FCT minister before they reconciled to form the Rainbow Coalition. Cole, speaking further, said he and Wike had put their past disagreements behind them and were now working towards a common political objective. “I believe politics is about sacrifice. There is no politician who does not have scars. But you have to be looking at the future. So today, Nyesom Wike and I do not have any differences. “What was in the past was in the past.

item.title: Stop recycling falsehoods against Tinubu, Lagos APC tells Pearse
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has slammed Dr. Adetokunbo Pearse over his recent series of interviews allegedly maligning and disparaging President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. Lagos State APC Spokesman, Seye Oladejo, who made the remark, described the statement as “an obsessive campaign of calumny,” against the President. The party said it would ordinarily have ignored the outbursts as a desperate attempt by a politically stranded individual to remain relevant, but added that the frequency, desperation and recycled nature of the allegations made it necessary to set the records straight. “There is something particularly unfortunate about a man who appears incapable of moving beyond yesterday’s political arguments, even when the issues he continues to resurrect have been exhaustively examined, contested and addressed through established legal and judicial processes,” the party stated. The APC said repetition does not transform an allegation into evidence, neither does the frequency with which a falsehood is circulated confer credibility upon it. “The Nigerian public is not obliged to accept recycled accusations simply because they are delivered with theatrical confidence in television studios,” it said. The party questioned how Pearse’s purported knowledge of the President’s academic history could be conclusive when, by his own account, he served at Chicago State University between 1985 and 1990, whereas President Tinubu’s academic records establish that he attended the institution between 1977 and 1979. “How does a lecturer who arrived at an institution six years after a student’s graduation become the ultimate authority on whether that student ever attended the institution?” the party asked. It described the discrepancy as not minor, saying “it goes to the very foundation of his latest claims,” adding that one would expect an academic of his purported standing to appreciate the importance of chronology, documentary evidence and elementary standards of verification. The party noted that the Chicago State University controversy is not a matter left to speculation, as the university itself has repeatedly confirmed President Tinubu’s attendance and graduation in 1979. It recalled that its Registrar, Caleb Westberg, also testified under oath in October 2023, confirming that the university’s official academic records showed that Bola Ahmed Tinubu graduated on June 22, 1979, with a degree in Business Administration. “These were not whispers in political corridors or claims made by hired political communicators. They were official institutional records and sworn testimony produced in the course of proceedings initiated at the instance of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar,” the party said. The APC said a responsible public commentator cannot conveniently ignore the university’s confirmation while presenting personal recollections, particularly recollections from a period several years after the President had

item.title: Uche Nnaji: HURIWA accuses ICPC of political persecution, demands halt to prosecution
item.description: … Alleges plot to weaken Mbah’s political challenger … Warns against weaponising anti-graft agencies ahead of 2027 elections By Chioma Obinna The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) on Friday accused the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) of using its prosecution of former Minister of Science, Technology and Innovation, Uche Nnaji, to advance political interests in Enugu State, demanding an immediate halt to the case pending an independent review. The rights group alleged that the continued prosecution of Nnaji, amid the controversy surrounding his academic qualifications, raises serious questions about the neutrality and independence of the anti-corruption agency, particularly as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a press statement signed by its National Coordinator, Comrade Emmanuel Nnadozie Onwubiko, HURIWA warned that criminal prosecution must not become an instrument for intimidating opposition figures, weakening political challengers or protecting incumbent office holders. The association alleged that Nnaji’s prosecution increasingly bears the appearance of a political project designed to undermine one of the formidable challengers to Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah. It claimed that the former minister remains one of the few politicians capable of mounting a serious challenge to Mbah’s political dominance, raising concerns that state institutions could be deployed to influence the state’s political landscape. HURIWA said: “The ICPC must stop this prosecution if it cannot convincingly establish that the process is independent, evidence-driven and free from political considerations. Nigerians must not allow persecution to disguise itself as prosecution.” The group maintained that while allegations against Nnaji should be subjected to lawful investigation and accountability, they must not provide a justification for selective deployment of state institutions against political actors. It also recalled that Nnaji had approached the Federal High Court to compel the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, to release his academic transcript, noting that the controversy surrounding his academic records remained contentious. According to HURIWA, the circumstances surrounding the investigation and prosecution require closer scrutiny to ensure that the anti-corruption agency is not acting on political considerations. The association further accused the Federal Government of failing to prevent anti-corruption institutions from operating in ways that could intimidate perceived political opponents and distort the country’s multiparty democratic process. Invoking the democratic principles underpinning the Electoral Act 2022, HURIWA argued that political competition must be free from intimidation, coercion and abuse of institutional power. It specifically cited Sections 126 and 127 of the Act, which address electoral offences involving force, violence, restraint, vote

item.title: Windows 11 passkey bug cries failure after successful sign-in
item.description: A Windows 11 passkey bug can leave Android phones announcing that authentication failed even when it succeeded. Microsoft has now released a fix for versions 25H2 and 26H2. The problem occurs when users sign in on a Windows 11 PC using a passkey stored on an Android phone. Scan the QR code, and the Android device might display the message: "Something went wrong. Restart the process on your other device and try again." Except it might not have gone wrong at all. Microsoft's guidance explains: "In cases where authentication completes successfully on the Windows device, the error message on the Android device is not supposed to appear and can be safely ignored." Cross-device authentication lets users sign in on one device using a passkey held on another, without typing a password or copying a verification code. Microsoft says the issue affects operations using Microsoft Authenticator and Google Password Manager, and can occur in Edge or Chrome – not just when signing in through Microsoft Entra ID. Cross-device passkey operations with an iPhone aren't affected. An authentication system that cries failure after a successful sign-in isn't doing much for user confidence. Nor will it endear itself to support teams fielding the resulting tickets. Microsoft has included a fix in KB5132057 , the optional non-security preview update released on November 19 for Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2. Until affected devices are patched, users can ignore the Android error if authentication has completed successfully on the PC. ®

item.title: AI is imposing a hidden ‘cognitive tax’ on the lowest-paid workers
item.description: It’s time to rethink welfare as AI reshapes the economy and wears down the brains of some of the most vulnerable workers AI is adding to the cognitive load of workers already stretched thin by unpredictable pay, insecure housing and mounting debt – and the lowest paid feel it most. We need to rethink welfare for an economy being reshaped by AI. Throughout the history of the study of economics, the human brain, which directs our labour, judgment and resilience, has rarely been considered an asset in its own right. The emerging AI economy is changing that. As machines take on routine work, what becomes most valuable is the judgment, creativity and insights only people can provide. Economists coined a term for this in recent years: brain capital. Professor Dame Henrietta Moore is founder and director of the UCL Institute for Global Prosperity and co-leads The New Alignment, the institute’s G20 policy programme Continue reading...

item.title: Einstein was right! Scientists verify 1st image of a black hole ever captured
item.description: null An independent team of researchers has validated the first image of a supermassive black hole captured by humanity. That, in turn, verifies Einstein's greatest theory, general relativity , which first predicted the existence of black holes and what their immediate surroundings would look like. Captured by a global network of telescopes forming an interferometer called the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) and revealed to the public in 2019, the image shows the supermassive black hole at the heart of the galaxy Messier 87 (M87), located 55 million light-years away. The image of this black hole , designated M87*, with a mass around 6.5 billion times that of the sun, was an immense scientific achievement. That may lead to the question: why did it need verifying at all? Team leader and researcher with Australia's Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO), Samuel Lai explained why capturing the image of a distant black hole is so tricky. "It is like standing in your backyard and trying to take a photo of a doughnut on the moon," Lai said in a statement sent to Space.com via email. Lai and his small Australian team developed advanced machine learning and artificial intelligence techniques to capture information about the black hole's structure and filter out interference resulting from the fact that the EHT was viewing M87* from within our planet's atmosphere. The machine-learning technique called GenDIReCT also accounted for biases introduced by combining telescopes to create an Earth-sized interferometer. "When we applied it to the original EHT dataset, we found a black hole almost identical in size and shape as the historic EHT image. Importantly, our model had no idea what a black hole looked like when we applied it to the M87 data," Lai continued. "This is the first truly independent validation of the EHT image, an important step in the scientific process." This could settle the questions of just how the final image of M87* was influenced by both atmospheric effects and the processing methods needed to reconstruct pictures from telescope data. That's not just good news for the EHT; it's good news for Einstein. Take it away Einstein Einstein published his theory of general relativity in 1915, completely reshaping how we think of gravity. General relativity suggested that objects with mass curve the very fabric of space and time, united as a single entity called spacetime. Gravity arises from that curvature. The greater the mass, the more extreme the curvature and thus the greater the gravitational influence of that object. Taking this to its extreme, scientist Karl Schwarzschild came up with a solution to the equations of general relativity that suggested an infinitesimal region with infinite mass, resulting in unrestrained curvature, a singularity. Around this would be a spherical boundary at which not even light has the velocity needed to escape this region. Referred to as the Schwarzschild radius, that boundary became

item.title: Watch SpaceX Dragon cargo capsule head home to Earth from the ISS today
item.description: null SpaceX's latest Drago cargo mission is scheduled to head back home toward Earth today (Nov. 20), and you can watch the action live. The robotic Dragon capsule will undock from the International Space Station (ISS) today at around 12:05 p.m. EST (1705 GMT), if all goes according to plan. You can watch Dragon's departure live here at Space.com, courtesy of NASA. Coverage will begin at 11:45 a.m. EST (1645 GMT). A SpaceX Dragon spacecraft supporting the company's 34th commercial resupply services mission for NASA departs the International Space Station on June 16, 2026. (Image credit: NASA/Jessica Meir) If Dragon does indeed leave the ISS today, it will splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on Saturday (Nov. 21) at about 4:55 p.m. EST (2155 GMT). There will be no livestream for its reentry and splashdown. A safe return to Earth requires relatively calm seas, so NASA and SpaceX are keeping a close eye on the weather in the splashdown zone. If conditions aren't great for a Saturday afternoon return, Dragon will stay docked to the ISS for a bit longer, until things improve. This particular Dragon launched Oct. 13, on a mission called CRS-35 because it's the 35th that SpaceX has flown for NASA's Commercial Resupply Services program. The capsule arrived at the ISS on Oct. 15 , delivering more than 6,300 pounds (2,860 kilograms) of food, scientific gear and other supplies to the astronauts aboard the orbiting lab. It will bring a lot of stuff down to Earth, too. "Thousands of pounds of cargo are returning from the space station, including research samples that could advance future space exploration and improve life on Earth," NASA officials wrote in an update on Tuesday (Nov. 17). "The returning research includes a 3D-bioprinted blood vessel construct scientists used to study vascular aging and cardiovascular disease in space and on Earth ," they added. Dragon is the only cargo craft flying today that's capable of making such downward deliveries. The others — Northrop Grumman's Cygnus, Russia's Progress vehicle and Japan's HTV-X — are all expendable and burn up in Earth's atmosphere to wrap up their first and only spaceflight.

item.title: ‎INEC releases 86,931 new PVCs for collection in Kogi
item.description: ‎By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja ‎‎The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Kogi State has announced the availability of 86,931 Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) for residents who participated in the second phase of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise. ‎The State Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) Dr. Shehu Wahab, made this known in a press statement made available to newsmen in Lokoja on Friday. ‎According to the commission, the second phase of the CVR exercise was conducted between January 5 and April 17, 2026. ‎‎INEC said, “The 86,931 PVCs produced for eligible registrants have been delivered to our offices across the 21 Local Government Areas of the state and are now ready for collection.” ‎‎The commission advised registrants to visit the INEC office in the Local Government Area where they completed their registration to collect their cards. ‎‎It said registrants are expected to come with their registration slips or printouts, or a valid means of identification where required. ‎‎INEC also clarified that PVCs from the first phase of the registration exercise are still available for collection. ‎‎”PVCs would not be issued through proxies, registrants must personally collect their cards. Collection is available at INEC LGA offices from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m., Monday to Friday.” ‎The commission further directed registrants to check the status of their PVCs and locate their collection centres through its CVR portal, cvr.inecnigeria.org. ‎‎INEC urged all voters who participated in the second phase of the CVR exercise to collect their PVCs without delay, noting that the cards are essential for participation in future elections. ‎‎The commission said timely collection would help ensure that no eligible voter is disenfranchised. ‎‎Wahab expressed appreciation to registrants for their patience during the production, verification and distribution processes, assuring that the commission remained committed to ensuring that every eligible voter obtains a PVC and is able to exercise their democratic right. The post ‎INEC releases 86,931 new PVCs for collection in Kogi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ADC, NDC, PDP, others halt campaigns, sign common agreement Nov 30
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Member parties of the Coalition for Democracy, among them the African Democratic Congress ADC, the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC and a faction of the Peoples Democratic Party PDP among others will suspend campaign activities nationwide on Monday, 30th November 2026, to attend the second summit of the coalition. The decision was announced in a statement issued on Friday and signed by Salihu Moh. Lukman on behalf of the coalition parties. According to him, concerned parties will sign a common agreement ahead of the January 16 presidential elections. The summit had been scheduled for Monday, 23rd November 2026, but Linkman said member parties asked that it be rescheduled because their candidates and campaign teams are now deep into demanding programmes across the country. “It is more important that every party, every presidential candidate and every national chairman is in the room than that the Summit holds on its original date,” the committee said. The committee said the new date was agreed in consultation with key stakeholders to secure the widest possible participation. To make that commitment real, all member parties agreed to suspend campaign activities nationwide on the day, so that their leadership can attend in full. “Parties competing hard for votes are prepared to stand down their campaigns for a day, together, because the defence of Nigeria’s democratic space is bigger than any one campaign,” it said. According to the statement, the summit will finalise and sign the coalition’s common agreement and set the course for the work ahead of the 16 January 2027 elections. The committee thanked member parties, delegates and partners for their understanding and regretted any inconvenience caused by the change. It said venue and accreditation details remain as communicated. The coalition emerged from the G100 Opposition Summit held in Abuja on 31 August 2026. It is a multiparty platform pioneered by the ADC, the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), the NDC, the PDP, the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) and the Social Democratic Party (SDP). The statement said it was established to give practical expression to the resolutions of that summit, and is committed to defending Nigeria’s constitutional democracy, protecting political pluralism, and ensuring free, fair, credible and competitive elections. It described the coalition as a framework for opposition parties to coordinate their efforts, safeguard democratic institutions, uphold the rule of law, and protect the fundamental rights of Nigerians to freely choose their leaders. “We will walk into that room united, and walk out of it committed,” the committee said. The post ADC, NDC, PDP, others halt campaigns, sign common agreement Nov 30 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: I’m a tech expert and new mum. Here’s what I learned testing 17 baby monitors
item.description: Our tech expert and new mum tested 17 monitors for picture quality, battery life and reliability – here’s what she recommends • The best eco-friendly baby products Moving my baby into her own room to sleep felt liberating and stressful. She was ready for her own space – but was I ready to let her out of my sight? Well, the first thing I did was buy a video baby monitor, so clearly I wasn’t. But it meant she could sleep peacefully in her new room and I could sneak a reassuring peek from afar whenever I felt the need. There’s a huge range of baby monitors, from simple audio-only options to sophisticated video models. Some even include wearables or other devices to track a baby’s breathing or heart rate, while others offer AI features to analyse sleep patterns. At their most basic, baby monitors typically consist of a baby unit, which you position near the baby, and a parent unit, which lets you hear and/or see them. With video models, the baby unit is essentially a camera, while the parent unit is a screen. Many are also wifi-enabled, meaning you can connect the monitor to your smartphone and view the live feed through an app instead of using a dedicated parent unit (read on for security advice). item.title: 2030: FG takes decisive action to end open defecation with Executive Order
item.description: By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA – IN a renewed commitment, the Federal Government has unveiled a new Executive Order to accelerate Nigeria’s drive towards ending open defecation by 2030. The unveiling of the Open Defecation Free Nigeria by 2030 and Other Related Matters Order, 2025 coincided with the commemoration of World Toilet Day and the seventh anniversary of the Clean Nigeria campaign in Abuja on Thursday. Vice President Kashim Shettima, represented by the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Delivery and Coordination in the Office of the Vice President, Akubo Adegbe, described the Executive Order as a decisive step towards translating government commitments into measurable sanitation outcomes. Shettima said the order marks a transition from fragmented interventions to stronger coordination, measurable results and sustainable national progress. He called on state and local governments to strengthen accountability, increase sanitation financing and sustain community-led behavioural change He disclosed that since the launch of the Clean Nigeria campaign in 2019, 185 of the country’s 774 local government areas have attained Open Defecation Free (ODF) status, while Jigawa and Katsina remain the only states certified as ODF nationwide. While acknowledging the progress recorded, the Vice President warned that the country still had considerable ground to cover, urging states yet to achieve ODF status to establish monthly and quarterly targets and make their progress publicly available. He also cautioned against a reversal of gains in communities already certified as open defecation-free, stressing the need for sustained monitoring and accountability to protect existing achievements. According to him, Nigeria must prioritise sustainable financing, reliable data, stronger institutions, effective implementation and continuous behavioural change to achieve the 2030 target. He also called on state and local governments to take ownership of the campaign by allocating adequate resources and strengthening sanitation institutions, while urging development partners, the private sector, traditional rulers, community leaders and civil society organisations to sustain their support. Shettima, who chairs the Steering Committee of the Clean Nigeria Project, reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to working with subnational governments, noting that the National Economic Council would also be deployed to advance and sustain the national sanitation agenda. Linking the campaign to this year’s World Toilet Day theme, “Sanitation and Gender Equality,” the Vice President highlighted the disproportionate burden poor sanitation places on women and girls. He noted that inadequate access to safe and private sanitation facilities undermines their health, security, dignity, education and participation in economic and social activities. item.title: Good night Olufemi Ajasa, you were more than a friend
item.description: By Taiwo George During the launch of the Converged Digital Newsroom of Media Trust Group, Alhaji Mohammed Idris, Minister of information and National Orientation, shared a personal story. While tracing the success story of the company, the Minister who was Special Guest at the occasion, narrated an encounter he had with Malam Kabir Yusuf, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Media Trust Group. According to him, several decades ago, he and Media Trust Chairman had a sit-down session in Kaduna and Malam Yusuf told him about his dream of owning a successful media outfit, while he, the Minister, told Malam Kabiru of his own dream to be a Public Relations merchant. If there is anyone whom I shared my dream in this profession with, it was Olufemi. But because tomorrow is not promised to anyone, I unlike the Minister, would not have the opportunity to ever watch my late brother and colleague relieve a similar encounter in future. Kabi o osi! Femi and I shared many things in common. We attended same institution, though while he was at the Communication School of the Lagos State University (LASU) in Anthony, I was at the main campus in Ojo. We got admitted the same year and graduated same year. Our marital journey also has striking similarities. His wife and mine are both Mass Communicators. Our spouses were first colleagues before signing lifetime contract. While Femi met his wife at Uni, I met mine during the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) programme. At death, Femi was the Online Editor of Vanguard, I’m currently the Online Editor of Daily Trust. Both of us are not just proud sons of Lagos, but we share ancestral ties. This is why it’s still quite difficult to come to terms with his sudden demise. A man of few words. He moved on whenever he made his point. Femi was never the one who would bore you with a conversation. Each time we spoke on phone, he went straight to the point. The few times the conversation dragged I said let me quickly make this final point, he would respond, “Oya na!”, and follow up with, “Take care!” whenever I summarized my point. Something unusual happened on the eve of his death. We usually compared notes on so many issues, particularly work. I came across an information which had to do with his workplace and forwarded same message to him via WhatsApp but it didn’t deliver. An online Editor being offline during that period? I assumed he was in a place where network was bad, and would respond when he read the message until Monday morning when Victor Ogunyinka, our mutual friend, broke the news to me. I screamed and my wife who was coincidentally sleeping on the same couch Femi and his family sat when they attended the parlour party during my son’s third-year birthday, woke up. I told her what happened and she regained consciousness immediately. We went over a few memories with Femi and said prayers for the wife and kids he left behind. item.title: Ubuntu Core Desktop targets 28.04 debut, with default status in its sights
item.description: Canonical is targeting Ubuntu 28.04 LTS for the release of its immutable Core Desktop, with a stretch goal of making it the default download for Ubuntu 30.04. Canonical's VP of engineering, Jon Seager, set out the timetable in his opening keynote at Ubuntu Summit 26.10. Yes, we know, we have heard this before: we reported on his plans last month . But this time, there's the beginning of a release schedule. Seager said that Ubuntu Core is already out there in tens of thousands of IoT devices – which seems like a modest estimate to us, and to him too, as he quickly added "maybe more." Despite some noise a few years ago, though, what's still missing is the desktop version. Seager's slides listed three bullet points: that Core Desktop will be "immutable," "composable," and "attestable." As he put it, they are "taking the whole of the Linux operating system, and cramming the whole thing into snaps." Acknowledging that this is going to be wildly controversial, he said: "This is one for the Redditors." He's right. There is a lot of resistance to snap, and in direct response, advocacy of the Red Hat-backed Flatpak instead – but we have seen almost none that is based on either system's technical merits. Much of that opposition concerns claims of one being more open than the other. We've looked at how both systems work, and our impression is that the implementation of snap is cleaner, simpler, easier to use, and more comprehensible. Snap does depend on systemd, which Flatpak does not – but only for now. Flatpak NG is in development and will also need everyone's favorite init system. Ubuntu Core's immutability is not new technology: even Core 16 is now a decade old. It has supported in-place version upgrades since Core 22. We have reported before that Canonical remains strongly committed to its packaging format, and that commitment seems stronger than ever. Seager continued: "Never has a model like snap confinement been more relevant… we're finally in a position where we can bring this to the desktop." The core idea of an immutable OS is that "much more of the system is not writable at runtime," meaning that it "can't be messed with once the system has booted." He talked about the same three use cases we discussed last month. The "browser-centric machine" is the company's analog to Google ChromeOS, and he said that it's essentially ready now, suggesting that everyone listening probably has a family member whose computer is basically just a way to use a web browser. The second was the dedicated games machine, which we interpret as a response to Valve's SteamOS. This edition, he said, would "boot straight to Steam," with "just enough of a shell to launch games." There's also an immutable "development workstation," and here, he offered the example of developers who need to work on some long-unsupported hardware or software, for whom an immutable OS means that you "can't brick your system by installing some weird old dependencies, unmaintained for 20 years." ‘There Are People Telling Tinubu Lies About Nigerians’ Support,’ Says Baba-Ahmed
item.description: The National Chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, has accused some political loyalists of misleading President Bola Tinubu about the level of public support for his administration. Baba-Ahmed, who once served under the Tinubu administration as Special Adviser on Political Matters in the Office of the Vice President, said the president’s associates could be giving him a false impression of his popularity by relying on assurances from governors and party loyalists rather than listening to ordinary Nigerians. He made the remarks on Friday during an appearance on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief programme. The PRP chairman said his assessment of public sentiment was based on his grassroots political connections and familiarity with the administration, which he initially supported. “I’m a politician. I lead a political party that is entirely grassroots-based. I have very strong organic links with the people. I followed the Tinubu administration from inception. Initially, I was even part of it,” he said. ﻿ Baba-Ahmed said he was familiar with the feelings of Nigerians and was not exaggerating the widespread dissatisfaction with the government. He identified poverty, economic mismanagement, corruption and insecurity as some of the issues contributing to the growing distance between the administration and the people. He also suggested that some political associates were giving Tinubu assurances about his chances of securing re-election in 2027 without adequately reflecting the mood of Nigerians. “There are a lot of people who are telling President Tinubu lies if he thinks himself, and they think that the people are with them. Just look at wherever APC goes. People either chase them away or they trigger violence,” he said. ‘Bamayi’ Baba-Ahmed also described the ‘Bamayi’ chants directed at the president as an expression of widespread dissatisfaction, insisting that the sentiment was not restricted to young people or northern Nigerians. “This Bamayi thing, it’s not just a slogan that young people throw at APC. It’s genuinely an organic element of the way Nigerians, not just northerners, Nigerians feel,” he added. The ‘Bamayi’ chants, which translate to ‘we don’t want’ in Hausa, were heard on November 13 after Tinubu attended Friday prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in the Garki area of Abuja. Some protesters reportedly threw stones at the president’s convoy and destroyed APC campaign posters, prompting security operatives to intervene. The incident attracted reactions from political figures, including Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain Segun Sowunmi, who condemned the protesters’ actions. Sowunmi, who is also a member of the APC campaign council, criticised the destruction of campaign posters and the use of violence during an appearance on Channels Television’s *Politics Today* on Monday. item.title: The BepiColombo spacecraft is finally entering orbit around Mercury
item.description: Artist’s impression of BepiColombo orbiting Mercury ESA/ATG medialab After a long and ponderous journey, the BepiColombo spacecraft will finally enter Mercury’s orbit on 21 November. Over the course of the next year, it will investigate the planet’s geology, its tenuous atmosphere and its magnetic field in an effort to understand how it formed and evolved over time. BepiColombo , a joint mission of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), launched in October 2018. Mercury’s proximity to the sun makes it incredibly difficult to reach without overshooting the planet and falling into the sun, so the spacecraft had to take a long and looping path over the past eight years, flying past both Venus and Mercury several times and using their gravity to make subtle tweaks to its trajectory. In 2024, an issue with the thrusters lengthened that journey even further, pushing the arrival date back from 2025 to 2026. Now, it has finally arrived. Read more 6 of the most fascinating moments in the life of our solar system While it is arriving at Mercury as a single spacecraft, BepiColombo actually comprises two separate orbiters: ESA’s Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO, or Mio). In December, the two will split apart and move to different orbits – MPO on a near-circular path that takes 2.3 hours to complete an orbit, and Mio on a more distant elliptical orbit, where it will take 9.3 hours to circle Mercury. Advertisement Those split orbits complement the differing scientific objectives of the two spacecraft. MPO is more than twice the size of MMO, and its 11 scientific instruments focus largely on studying Mercury itself . Its instruments include several types of spectrometer to measure the makeup of the surface, a laser altimeter to map its terrain and instruments to study the makeup of Mercury’s extremely thin atmosphere, called an exosphere. Mio’s more distant orbit will allow it to study a broader area around Mercury. It has five sets of scientific instruments to study the magnetic field and atmosphere of the planet, as well as the solar wind that blows strongly in the area close to the sun. Free newsletter Sign up to Launchpad Sign up to newsletter Now that the BepiColombo spacecraft are entering orbit, their primary mission is expected to last only one Earth year, which is a little more than four Mercury years. The mission could potentially be extended for another year, but beyond that the combination of limited fuel and extreme temperatures will make it all but impossible to keep going. Over the course of the year, researchers hope that BepiColombo will provide enough data to solve some of Mercury’s many mysteries. Mercury’s magnetic field is bewildering, because it originates 400 kilometres above the planet’s centre and should have faded away long ago. Its atmosphere must be continuously supplied with material from the surface, but we are unsure exactly how that occurs.

item.title: Support tech fixed malware by charging client less for their services
item.description: Welcome to Friday and therefore to another edition of On Call , The Register 's reader-contributed tech support column in which we share your tales of cleaning up messes made by clients and colleagues. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Dennis" who told us he once ran a tech support business in a major US city. "I got a call from a very well-known lawyer's office," he told On Call. "Over the two decades I spent supporting his office, this attorney and I became close friends." The attorney was also a good client because Dennis found himself billing a three-figure sum every month for malware removal that resulted from the lawyer’s – ahem – personal browsing habits. Dennis eventually tired of malware removal and told his client to expect a substantial bill for the iMac he was about to buy as a replacement for his PC. "I told him this would pay for itself in 18 months," Dennis wrote, because he figured it wouldn't get malware all the time. "He actually said, with genuine concern: 'If you do that, you will make less money'." Dennis replied that he aimed to give his clients the best advice, and that on this occasion his counsel was to pay Apple instead of himself! "It took him about five years to stumble across anything that could harm that iMac," Dennis wrote. "When he did, I had no idea what to do: I had never seen an infected Apple product." So he did what all tech support people do: reinstalled the OS and crossed his fingers. Dennis was rewarded when the machine came back to life, with all data and settings intact. "I had given up at least $6,000 in support revenue by solving his problem and I'd do it again," he wrote, before winding up his story by letting us know "I retired five years ago. It’s still on his desk!" Have you done less tech support to deliver more value? If so, click here to send On Call an email and charge us with the responsibility of telling your story on a future Friday. ®

item.title: Nigeria, Russia move to ease trade, strengthen customs cooperation
item.description: By Providence Ayanfeoluwa The Nigeria Customs Service, NCS and Federal Customs Service of Russia have signed a cooperation agreement aimed at strengthening bilateral trade facilitation, intelligence sharing and customs enforcement, while exploring mutual recognition of their Authorised Economic Operator, AEO programmes. The service in a statement said the Agreement on Cooperation and Mutual Assistance in Customs Matters, CMAA provides a framework for collaboration in customs procedures, information exchange, financial integrity, border security and personnel capacity development. Speaking, Comptroller-General of Customs, Adewale Adeniyi, who led the Nigerian delegation, described the agreement as a strategic instrument for safeguarding economic integrity, securing supply chains and strengthening trade governance. He explained that the signing followed months of technical consultations, legal reviews and constructive engagements between both administrations. Adeniyi explained that the NCS had accelerated its digital transformation through the adoption of electronic systems for customs declarations, payments and submission of supporting documents. According to him, the reforms demonstrate that revenue generation and trade facilitation can complement each other, in line with the World Customs Organisation’s SAFE Framework of Standards. On the implementation of the agreement, the Customs boss identified cooperation between the two countries’ AEO programmes as a major priority. He said both administrations would exchange experiences on their respective frameworks and operational procedures, with the long-term objective of achieving mutual recognition to facilitate the movement of cargo and reward compliant traders. The two sides also explored arrangements for exchanging customs statistics and trade data to improve analysis of bilateral trade flows. Adeniyi disclosed that Nigeria was participating in the World Customs Organisation’s data initiative. Russia’s Head of Customs, Valery Pikalyov, explained that his administration was authorised to collect and exchange customs statistics derived from declarations. Pikalyov expressed readiness to explore a dedicated data-sharing arrangement with Nigeria. The agreement also provides for cooperation against customs offences, illicit financial flows, grey-market importations, tax evasion, counterfeit goods, narcotics and other prohibited or hazardous materials. It further establishes a framework for direct operational assistance, personnel training and the exchange of professional expertise between the two administrations. The post Nigeria, Russia move to ease trade, strengthen customs cooperation appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 20, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian naira continued to face downward pressure against the United States dollar across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market on Friday, November 20, 2026, driven by tightening foreign exchange supply and rising end-of-year seasonal demand. Official Market Performance Real-time interbank spot tracking at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market placed the US dollar at ₦1,352.54 during early morning trading on Friday, following an opening rate of ₦1,351.86 and an intraday peak of ₦1,355.31. This early session trading follows Thursday’s official Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) volume-weighted benchmark, which saw the naira depreciate to a four-month low. According to official CBN data for the November 19 trading session, the NFEM weighted average rate settled at ₦1,376.58 per dollar, while the indicative closing rate rose to ₦1,388.00 per dollar from ₦1,379.99 recorded on Wednesday. Intraday interbank transactions on Thursday were conducted between a low of ₦1,370.00 and a high of ₦1,397.00 per dollar. Despite the depreciation, market liquidity improved significantly, with NFEM interbank turnover surging by 59.13 percent to $800.31 million across 184 deals, up from $502.88 million the previous day. Parallel Market Rates In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the local currency weakened further as Bureau de Change (BDC) operators and street dealers in Lagos and Abuja quoted the US dollar at a selling rate of up to ₦1,468 per dollar on Friday morning, following Thursday’s close between ₦1,461 and ₦1,468. Buying rates among informal currency dealers hovered between ₦1,445 and ₦1,458 depending on transaction volume and location. With Thursday’s official closing benchmark at ₦1,388.00 and parallel market quotations reaching ₦1,468.00, the spread between the official and unofficial windows widened to ₦80.00 per dollar, compared to ₦70.01 recorded earlier in the week. Market Drivers and Reserve Outlook Since the end of October, when the naira closed at ₦1,346.00 in the official window and ₦1,373.00 in the parallel market, the currency has lost ₦42.00 and ₦95.00 in the respective segments. Meanwhile, Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $54.71 billion as of November 18, 2026, reflecting a moderation of $554 million from the October 27 peak of $55.26 billion. item.title: Why we pulled down Umeh’s billboard — Anambra govt
item.description: The Anambra State Government has dismissed claims that a billboard belonging to Senator Victor Umeh was pulled down because it carried the image of former Governor Peter Obi, calling the allegation false and misleading. The government said the enforcement action stemmed from an alleged violation of the Anambra State Signage Act, 2010, rather than the identity or political affiliation of anyone featured on the billboard. In a statement issued yesterday, the Commissioner for Information and Value Reformation, Dr Law Mefor, said that although Senator Umeh had paid the required signage fee, Peter Obi had not complied with the payment requirement. Mefor alleged that the senator, instead of fully complying with the law, used the billboard to promote the presidential candidate of the New Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), thereby contravening the state’s signage regulations. He stressed that the removal was carried out strictly in accordance with the law, which he noted was enacted during Peter Obi’s administration as governor of Anambra State. “For the avoidance of doubt, the billboard was not pulled down because of Peter Obi’s image,” the commissioner stated. The government further warned that any combined billboard campaign featuring candidates who had not fulfilled their signage obligations would face similar enforcement, regardless of their political party, status, or affiliation. It maintained that the state’s outdoor advertising regulations would be guided by fairness, transparency, and even-handed application of the law. Mefor urged the public to disregard what he described as a misleading narrative surrounding the incident, insisting that the government remained committed to due process and equal treatment in enforcing existing laws. item.title: 53 Years Later, The Greatest Closing Line In Sci-Fi History Is Still The Best Book Quote Of The 1970s
item.description: The canon of science-fiction literature is home to countless unforgettable endings, from 1984 ’s short but devastating retrospective ("He loved Big Brother") to The Three-Body Problem ’s defiant reminder that humanity cannot be so easily wiped out. The best sci-fi endings don't offer comfortable closure. Instead, they reframe everything that came before. In their closing lines, great sci-fi novelists leave readers suspended in the aftermath, forced to stew in the terrifying logic of cold technology, the fragility of human nature, and the vast expanse of space.

item.title: ESUT to be renamed after Jim Nwobodo – Mbah
item.description: Governor of Enugu State, Dr. Peter Mbah, has unveiled plans to rename the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT) after a Second Republic Governor of old Anambra State, Senator Jim Nwobodo, subject to stakeholders engagement and legislative due process. Mbah made this known during the 3rd Distinguished Personality Lecture of the university delivered by Nwobodo at the Barr. Peter Ndubuisi Mbah Multipurpose Auditorium, ESUT, Enugu, on Thursday. He said the idea, which was first suggested by the ESUT Alumni Association, was in tandem with his thoughts, describing it as a fitting tribute to the elder statesman, who founded the institution in 1980. The Governor emphasised that the brainchild of the ex-governor had played a critical role in the human capital development of not just Enugu State, but also the old Anambra State and Nigeria as a whole. “Recently, representatives of the alumni of this university and its associated institutions came to see me. “They asked that Enugu State University of Science and Technology be renamed in honour of Senator Jim Ifeanyichukwu Nwobodo. “I told them that I support the proposal. I was particularly encouraged that the request came from the alumni who understand, through their own experience, what the university has meant to people’s lives. “There is a legal process to follow. ESUT was established by law, and changing its name would require the appropriate legislative steps and engagement with relevant stakeholders. “I intend to begin those engagements and work with the institutions concerned to advance the proposal through the proper process. “Your Excellency, I hope that gives you some sense of the regard in which your contribution continues to be held.” The Governor praised Nwobodo’s vision and courage in leadership, especially for investing heavily in human capital development, taking the bold step to establish ESUT a few years after the civil war, not minding the enormity of the challenges involved. “I have often wondered what it must have felt like to be governor in 1979. Nigeria had just returned to civilian government after thirteen years of military rule. “The Civil War had ended less than a decade earlier, and the country was still dealing with its consequences. There was much to rebuild, and enormous pressure on the resources available to government. “For many families, university education remained beyond their reach. And here was a young governor, who decided that his state should establish a university of science and technology. “People questioned whether it could be done. Was there enough money? Could a state government sustain such an institution? Shouldn’t this be left to the federal government? “These were reasonable questions. I suspect some of them would have kept you awake at night. “But for Jim Nwobodo, the fact that a problem is difficult does not mean we can afford to avoid it. “In July 1980, Anambra State University of Technology was established. item.title: Farmer allegedly macheted over grazing dispute in Benue
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi A farmer, identified as Mr Terkura Orvanya, has reportedly been macheted by suspected herdsmen following a disagreement over the grazing of cattle on his cultivated farm at Ikpakena village, Makurdi Local Government Area of Benue State. Orvanya was said to have sustained serious machete wounds while attempting to defend himself against one of the herders after challenging them for allowing their cattle to destroy his melon farm. The incident was made public by Joseph Apahar, Media and Publicity Officer of IDP Benue State, in a social media post. According to Apahar, two herders were grazing their cattle on Orvanya’s melon farm when the farmer arrived and asked them to remove the animals from his cultivated crops. He alleged that the herders, despite being aware that the farm belonged to the farmer, showed no concern and refused to move the cattle away. Apahar said trouble started when Orvanya attempted to chase the animals out of his farm, prompting one of the herders to allegedly draw a cutlass and attack him. He said the farmer sustained machete wounds while attempting to shield himself from the attack, adding that Orvanya was receiving medical attention at a private hospital. Expressing concern over the incident, Apahar lamented what he described as the increasing cases of herders allowing their cattle to destroy cultivated crops, particularly farms containing crops ready for harvest or already harvested. He noted that such incidents were becoming increasingly common in the area, describing the development as a recurrence of the annual clashes between farmers and herders during harvest seasons after a period of relative peace. Apahar appealed to security agencies to urgently intervene to protect farmers and their investments from further destruction. “We are appealing to the security agencies to intervene urgently and help secure our crops before we are forced out of our villages, losing everything, and thereby reduced to nothing,” he said. He stressed that farmers should be allowed to harvest their crops without intimidation or attacks, insisting that their lives and livelihoods must be protected. “Our farmers deserve to harvest in peace. Our lives and livelihoods must be protected,” Apahar added. Efforts to reach the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, for comments on the incident were unsuccessful, as he could not be reached at the time of filing this report. item.title: FG targets raw mineral export ban, revenue tops N100bn
item.description: By Gabriel Ewepu The Federal Government is pushing to end the export of unprocessed solid minerals as part of efforts to deepen local value addition, boost industrialisation and create jobs, even as revenue from the sector crossed N100 billion in 2026. President Bola Tinubu stated this yesterday at the Nigeria Now! Investing in Energy, Infrastructure and Mining Summit in Abuja, themed, “United Nigeria, New Horizons, One Investment Destination.” Tinubu said Nigeria was determined to move beyond exporting raw mineral resources, stressing the need for investment in processing and beneficiation to strengthen domestic industries. “In mining, we’re equally determined to move beyond the export of unprocessed resources. Better geological information, transparent licensing, responsible exploration, and greater investment in beneficiation and processing must support Nigerian industries, skilled employment and meaningful benefits for host communities,” he said. The President said the government was working to build integrated value chains that would enable Nigerian enterprises to participate more actively in the mining industry and expand domestic capabilities. He urged investors to bring technology, finance and commercial expertise, assuring them of efforts to strengthen regulatory certainty and institutional support for sustainable returns. Earlier, Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dr Dele Alake, said reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration had increased revenue from the sector from N6 billion annually before the administration to N100 billion in 2026. “When I assumed office, the sector’s total annual revenue stood at just N6 billion. However, through reforms, the local value addition policy, the digitisation of mining processes, and efforts to sanitise operations within the sector, that figure increased from N6 billion to N38 billion by 2024. “By 2025, it had risen to N70 billion. And just about a week ago, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) informed us that we had crossed the N100 billion mark this year,” Alake said. He attributed the growth to reforms and efforts to sanitise mining operations, including the establishment of Mining Marshals, which he said had apprehended over 300 illegal operators and recovered more than 100 mining sites. Meanwhile, Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Gboyega Oyetola, said revenue generated by agencies under his ministry rose from N700.79 billion in 2023 to N1.83 trillion in 2025. He cited improvements in maritime security, port reforms and approval of Nigeria’s first National Policy on Marine and Blue Economy, while urging investors to explore opportunities in shipping, ports, shipbuilding, fisheries, aquaculture and logistics. item.title: Tinubu reiterates commitment to respecting court judgments
item.description: By Henry Ojelu President Bola Tinubu, yesterday, reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to respecting court judgments. He also conferred the Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger, GCON, Nigeria’s second-highest national honour, on renowned lawyer, Chief Wole Olanipekun, SAN. President Tinubu at the launch of a six-volume book, Wole Olanipekun Through the Cases, organised to celebrate the senior lawyer’s 75th birthday, 50 years at the Bar and 35 years as an SAN, said: “Our administration respects court judgments, even the ones we do not enjoy reading. We do not denigrate, attack or intimidate the judiciary. A government that bullies its judges only weakens its own foundation. “This administration passed the Judicial Officeholder Salary and Allowances Act 2024, reversing over 15 years of stagnation and delivering a 300 percent increase in the salaries of our Judicial Officers of the Superior Court of record. “We are not yet at our desired designation. But significant work is in progress, and the brighter future is now in closer view. We will be there, my Lordship. Our administration respects court judgment, even the one we do not enjoy reading. “We do not denigrate, attack or intimidate the judiciary,” President Tinubu reassured. Tinubu urged stakeholders in the justice sector to promote Nigeria as a business-friendly destination, stressing that timely judgments could strengthen investor confidence. “Every timely judgment is an advertisement for the Nigerian economy,” he said. He congratulated Olanipekun on his professional milestones, noting that the senior lawyer had positively impacted Nigeria and humanity through his legal practice and mentorship. Tinubu described Olanipekun as a phenomenal Nigerian and outstanding advocate who had upheld the traditions of excellence in the legal profession. The President also acknowledged the lawyer’s decades of loyalty and friendship, disclosing that Olanipekun had led his legal team for decades. “On a personal note, I celebrate decades of loyalty, friendship, commitment and reciprocity between Wole Olanipekun and I. He has led my legal team for decades. In politics, friends come and go. Wole came, and Wole stayed,” he said. Tinubu said Olanipekun also led the legal teams that defended three of his predecessors when their election victories were challenged. He said the senior lawyer had consequently served as lead counsel to four successive Nigerian presidents since 2007, describing the record as unprecedented. “Presidents change. Parties change. The Lead Counsel remains,” he said. President of the Senate Godswill Akpabio lauded President Tinubu for his commitment to justice, democracy, and national development. He assured the President that the National Assembly will continue to support all legal instruments that will promote justice, democracy and the rule of law. item.title: Dangote cement records 60% reduction in road traffic accidents
item.description: Dangote Cement Plc. has recorded a remarkable 60 per cent reduction in road traffic accidents, following the implementation of a comprehensive driver safety programme, underscoring the company’s unwavering commitment to protecting lives and promoting road safety across its transportation operations. The milestone was announced at the 2026 Customer Truck Scheme, CTS, Annual Driver Safety Award and Recognition Programme, where the company celebrated drivers who demonstrated exemplary safety performance and maintained accident-free records throughout the assessment period. The achievement builds on an earlier 30 percent reduction in road traffic accidents recorded in 2023, following the introduction of the company’s Safety Improvement Plan. As part of the initiative, approximately 3,000 drivers were trained in defensive driving techniques and safe road-use practices. According to the company, the sustained decline in accidents reflects the effectiveness of continuous driver training, behavioural monitoring, corrective interventions, and the deliberate recognition of safe driving practices. Speaking at the event on behalf of the Group Sales and Marketing Director, the National Sales Director of Dangote Cement Plc, Mr. Dolapo Ali, noted that the rapid expansion of the company’s transportation operations had made road safety a critical business priority. He disclosed that the CTS fleet had grown significantly from 469 trucks in 2017 to over 2,500 trucks today, increasing the need for a more structured and proactive safety management approach. “Our business has experienced tremendous growth over the years, and with that growth comes greater responsibility. As the number of trucks and drivers operating across our roads increases, so too does our exposure to road safety risks. Protecting lives and ensuring safe operations must therefore remain at the heart of our transport strategy,” he stated. Ali explained that road traffic accidents peaked in 2021 and 2022, prompting the company to introduce its Safety Improvement Plan in early 2023. A key component of the programme was an intensive defensive-driving training initiative through which approximately 3,000 drivers received professional safety training. The intervention delivered immediate results, with accident rates declining by 30 per cent in 2023 compared to the previous year, followed by a further 60 per cent reduction thereafter. To strengthen compliance and encourage safer driving behaviour, Dangote Cement also deployed advanced telematics technology across its fleet operations. The system enables real-time monitoring of critical driving behaviours, including overspeeding, harsh braking, and aggressive acceleration. item.title: Dollar scarcity, festive demand push Naira to N1,468/$
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe & Elizabeth Adegbesan The naira yesterday continued its downward trend in both segments of the foreign exchange market, depreciating to N1,468 per dollar in the parallel market from N1,450 per dollar on Wednesday, as dwindling dollar supply and rising demand ahead of the festive season intensified pressure on the currency. Similarly, the naira weakened to N1,388 per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, NFEM, from N1,379.99 per dollar on Wednesday, representing a depreciation of N8.01. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, showed that the indicative exchange rate in the official market rose to N1,388 per dollar. Consequently, the gap between the parallel and official markets widened to N80 per dollar from N70.01 per dollar on Wednesday. Meanwhile, interbank turnover in the NFEM rose by 59.13 per cent to $800.3 million from $502.9 million recorded on Wednesday. Vanguard analysis showed that the naira has depreciated by N95 in the parallel market since October 31, when it closed at N1,373 per dollar. Similarly, the currency has depreciated by N42 in the official market from N1,346 per dollar at the end of October. The nation’s external reserves also declined to $54.71 billion on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, according to CBN data, representing a decline of $554 million from the peak of $55.264 billion recorded on October 27, 2026. Commenting on the development, Chief Investment Officer of VNL Capital Asset Management, Dr. Ubah Jeremiah, said the naira’s weakness was driven more by tightening dollar supply and rising seasonal demand than by significant depletion of external reserves. He said foreign exchange inflows had fallen sharply to about $807.6 million in the latest week from $2.48 billion previously, reducing dollar availability in the market. “With fewer dollars coming in from autonomous sources, the market has leaned more heavily on CBN supply just as importers, businesses, and individuals step up purchases ahead of the festive season and year-end obligations,” he said. Ubah also blamed diverging monetary policy positions between the CBN and the US Federal Reserve for reinforcing pressure on the naira, noting that higher US yields and a stronger dollar could weaken the attractiveness of naira assets and encourage portfolio outflows. Meanwhile, parallel-market trader, Jubril Yinusa, attributed the depreciation to rising demand and limited dollar supply. “The naira has recorded continuous depreciation this week due to the high demand as the festive season approaches and low supply. Importation demand is also contributing to the depreciation of the naira,” he said. Another trader, Isa Dauda, said the festive season and the forthcoming election were also contributing to pressure on the currency. He said some foreign investors were adopting a wait-and-see attitude ahead of the elections, further limiting foreign exchange inflows. item.title: ‘He was a go-getter’ – Taiwo Obe, Providus Bank mourn Ajasa
item.description: THE Chairman and founder of Journalism Clinic, Mr Taiwo Obe, has described the late Online Editor of Vanguard Newspapers, Mr Femi Ajasa, as a go-getter, regretting that his death has robbed journalism of one of its brightest young professionals. Similarly, Providus Bank, one of Nigeria’s new-generation banks, has expressed sadness over Ajasa’s demise, saying his death is a loss not only to Vanguard but also to the media industry. In a condolence letter by its Group Head, Brand and Corporate Communication, Dafe Ivwurie, the bank said: “We were deeply saddened to learn of the death of Olufemi Ajasa. “By all accounts, he was an accomplished and highly respected digital journalist whose professionalism, dedication, and commitment to excellence contributed immensely to the growth and reputation of Vanguard’s digital media platforms. His passing at such a young age is a great loss not only to Vanguard but also to the Nigerian media industry.” Meanwhile, Obe, who took to his Facebook page to mourn Ajasa, described him as one of the first journalists trained at his clinic. He recounted the events that brought him close to the deceased and traced the history of their relationship until Ajasa’s death on Sunday. Obe said: “Circa 1997, TaijoWonukabe Limited, which I co-founded about two years earlier, moved from its garage office graciously donated to us by the prolific columnist, late Pini Jason Onyegbadue, into a three-bedroom bungalow on Bassie Ogamba Street, off Adeniran Ogunsanya, in Surulere, Lagos. “That property belonged to Madam Pemu, a relation of Sam Amuka-Pemu, the legendary journalist, Uncle Sam. “One day, not long after we moved in, Uncle Sam showed up, to greet Madam Pemu, who lived in a separate bungalow on the same premises. “I knew him then more by name than physical interactions. Either when he was leaving or as he alighted, I approached him, to introduce myself and after we exchanged pleasantries, he said: Money is good. See how you boys have changed this building. “From that day till date, we became connected. Fast forward to circa 2015: I had founded The Journalism Clinic and converted and renamed the hall which was the finishing room of PrintPro Projects Limited – the printing subsidiary of TaijoWonukabe – to The Hub – the training room of The Journalism Clinic at Anifowose, around the corner from Bassie Ogamba. “Uncle Sam visited one afternoon and declared ‘Vanguard will send people to all the training you will do here’.” He kept his word and the first paid training we had in The Hub included three participants from Vanguard Online Desk and Olufemi Ajasa was one of them. “A fine gentleman, two days ago, Vanguard reported his passing after a brief illness. Since that training, I had encountered Femi in various places and positions. He remained as respectful as ever; always go-getting and consistently impeccably-dressed. This really hit hard. item.title: Tinubu moves to achieve 40% fares reduction under NACTP
item.description: President Bola Tinubu in his determination to achieve the 40 percent fare-reduction target under the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme NACTP, as outlined in his renewed hope agenda 2.0, has welcomed plans by Yutong, the world’s largest bus manufacturer and a global leader in electric and CNG-powered buses, to establish a CNG bus assembly plant in Nigeria. This followed his invitation to the Chinese automotive giant to support the expansion of affordable mass transportation across the country. Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, Mr. Bayo Onanuga, in a statement, yesterday, noted that the investment would support the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme, NACTP, in collaboration with state governments, which targets transport fare reductions of approximately 40 percent on participating routes, in line with the President’s renewed hope agenda 2.0 for 2027–2031. Under the agreement with the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles, Pi-CNG & EV, Yutong will supply an initial 300 CNG-powered buses, with the first 100 expected to arrive in Lagos by the end of December 2026. Subsequent buses will be assembled in Nigeria through YP Automobiles Bus Assembly at the former Leyland Automotive plant in Ibadan, Oyo State, reviving local industrial capacity, reducing dependence on imported vehicles and creating employment opportunities for Nigerian engineers, technicians and other workers. Yutong, which sold 49,518 buses globally in 2025, brings extensive experience in mass transit manufacturing, with operations across international markets and a track record of supporting local assembly and public transportation projects in several countries. The President noted that the investment comes as CNG adoption continues to increase nationwide, supported by the expansion of refuelling infrastructure through Pi-CNG & EV, the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund, MDGIF, and private sector investors. These interventions include deploying Mobile Refuelling Units (MRUs) and the President’s directive for 2,000 additional CNG refuelling infrastructure units nationwide, laying the foundation for a wider rollout of affordable commercial buses. President Tinubu emphasises that reducing the daily cost of transportation for Nigerians remains the central objective of these investments. The President notes that millions of Nigerians depend on commercial transportation to get to work, take their children to school, travel to markets and move goods between communities. For many households, transportation consumes a significant portion of their daily earnings. He stresses that the lower operating costs of CNG-powered vehicles must translate into lower fares for passengers, allowing workers, traders and families to retain more of their income for food, education and other essential needs. item.title: APOD: 2026 November 20 – V-G-R
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. V-G-R Explanation: On November 17, fans of interstellar spaceflight around planet Earth were invited to shine a message into the night sky. Traced by a flashlight beam switched on and off, the dashes and dots of a Morse code message captured in this time exposure from the Emirates Astronomical Observatory, are read V-G-R. That’s a call sign for the Voyager 1 spacecraft currently in interstellar space some 26 billion kilometers away. How long did it take the message to reach humanity’s most distant interstellar spacecraft ? Traveling at the speed of light, the answer is one day . In fact, the Voyager 1 spacecraft was confirmed to reach its one light-day distance milestone on November 18, at 10:16:07 UTC, nearly 50 years after launch in 1977. For extra credit, fans of math can calculate that at one light-day per 50 years, Voyager 1 will reach its one light-year (365 light-days) distance milestone in about 18,250 years.
